channel.title: Kubai Kevin
channel.description: Practical backend engineering, AI tooling, and developer career advice by Kubai Kevin — a software developer with 10+ years building production systems in fintech and AI.

item.title: PAPSS and mobile money: where integration breaks
item.description: Why cross-border PAPSS and mobile money integrations break: hold-and-resolve state machines, identifier resolution, and pending-set reconciliation.

item.title: Technical debt: defend priorities to stakeholders
item.description: A framework that turns technical debt into cost, risk, and timing arguments stakeholders can act on, with scoring, cost-of-delay arithmetic, and capacity rules.

item.title: BM25 vs dense embeddings: hybrid search reality
item.description: How BM25 and dense retrieval fail differently, why score fusion is not free, and how to choose RRF, weighted fusion, or a cascade for your corpus.

item.title: SQLAlchemy vs asyncpg: pooling in async services
item.description: How SQLAlchemy's async engine and asyncpg's pool actually relate, how to size pools against Postgres max_connections, and the failure modes that cause timeouts.

item.title: Gateway API won't fix your Ingress mess
item.description: Gateway API does not fix messy Ingress manifests. It changes who owns routing. Here is when delegation is worth the migration and when to wait.

item.title: Distroless images: smaller attack surface
item.description: How to move runtime containers to distroless bases, measure the reduction in packages and CVEs, and keep scans blocking in CI.

item.title: 3 LLM context techniques: when each fails
item.description: Compare fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation and long context by failure mode, cost arithmetic and a decision checklist, with code for each.

item.title: STRIDE is a checklist, not a threat model
item.description: STRIDE is a memory aid, not a threat model. Use attack trees to map paths to an asset and STRIDE to prompt each node, with a CI check that keeps trees current.

item.title: Small language models: the classifier trap
item.description: Why compact classifiers fail on rare inputs, and how per-label thresholds, guardrails and score monitoring contain the damage.

item.title: Dependency pinning: the lockfile lie
item.description: A lockfile records a resolution, not a guarantee. Learn where determinism breaks, how to enforce lockfiles in CI, and how pinning interacts with SCA.

item.title: KYC integrations: the data you shouldn't store
item.description: Design a KYC integration that persists only the decision and a vendor reference, with the raw identity evidence kept by the vendor under contract.

item.title: OpenTelemetry collector pipelines: sampling, batching…
item.description: How receivers, processors, and exporters interact under load, with worked memory arithmetic, sampling trade-offs, routing isolation, and metrics to watch.

item.title: Node.js memory leak: find it in 10 min
item.description: Classify rising memory before profiling it: compare heapUsed and rss, take two heap snapshots, read retainer paths, and bound every in-memory structure.

item.title: AI answers first, judgment later
item.description: AI assistants give juniors fast, confident answers without your system's context. Here is how to move mentoring from giving answers to reviewing judgment.

item.title: Database restore drills that mean something
item.description: A repeatable PostgreSQL restore drill that measures recovery time, data loss window and integrity, plus the failure modes that make drills lie.

item.title: Multi-agent DX: LangGraph vs CrewAI gaps
item.description: Where LangGraph and CrewAI leave you on your own when debugging multi-agent systems, the failure modes that recur, and how to instrument for causal traces.

item.title: JWT sessions: revocation, rotation, storage
item.description: Why JWT revocation is a state problem, how refresh token rotation with reuse detection works, and how token storage shapes the threat model.

item.title: Context engineering: the real fix for agent hallucinations
item.description: Long-running agents fail because their context fills with stale tool output and contradictions. Here is how to structure, prune and measure that context.

item.title: HPA vs KEDA vs Karpenter: autoscaling traps
item.description: How HPA, KEDA and Karpenter divide responsibility, where each one silently fails, and how to verify each layer before traffic arrives.

item.title: Drift detection: the plan that lies
item.description: Terraform plan only reports drift a provider reads back. Build observe-classify-remediate pipelines that catch out-of-band changes safely.
